claim: A 28 MHz hook in front of a tight loop can be slower than the loop when the per-byte saving is smaller than the hook's fixed entry and exit cost; replace the whole loop instead.

evidence.text: NOPing a plotter's stores saves only 3 T a byte, less than a hook's fixed entry and exit at 3.5 MHz (about 250 T), so a 28 MHz hook in front of the loop made the game slower (pace model +3,800 T a tick).
